newsitem.title: USA: Discount Auto Parts to post lawsuit charge.
newsitem.headline: Discount Auto Parts to post lawsuit charge.

text.p: Discount Auto Parts Inc said on Monday that it will post a $12 million after tax charge in fiscal 1997 to reflect a settlement of a lawsuit with Airgas Inc.

Airgas filed a lawsuit in February 1997 that alleged Discount Auto Parts took part in a conspiracy with other companies to defraud Airgas in connection with commercial sales of refrigerant freon, Discount Auto said in a statement.
In the settlement, there is no finding or admission of wrongdoing on the part of Discount Auto Parts.
Discount Auto said the charge will affect the results for the fourth quarter ended in May 1997. Those financial results will be reported in a few days, the company said.
Money to fund the settlement will come from a portion of the company's available borrowing capacity under its revolving credit facility, Discount Auto said.

Discount Auto said it is continuing to cooperate with federal investigations into the subject of this litigation, including a Savannah, Ga., grand jury proceeding and an informal Securities and Exchange Commission investigation.
Discount Auto said it entered the settlement because of the risks of defending complex litigation.

Under the specific terms of the settlement, Discount Auto Parts will purchase from Airgas Specialty Gases, on an "as is, where is" basis, approximately 6,500 cylinders believed to contain an alternative to R-12 refrigerant for an aggregate price of $4.0 million.

This represents a price that is believed by the company to be approximately $3.6 million in excess of the current market value of such product, Discount Auto said. In addition, Discount Auto Parts will pay an additional $13.0 million to Airgas Specialty Gases.

As a separate but related part of the settlement, Discount Auto Parts will pay $500,000 to the bankruptcy estate of Refrigeration Station to settle any claims it has against it and pay $1.0 million for 7,200 cylinders of a freon alternative, the company said.
If Airgas does not recover at least $1.5 million from the Refrigeration Station bankruptcy by January 2, 1998, Discount Auto Parts will also pay to Airgas any shortfall, Discount Auto said.
